rationale: This is a mechanical 2x2 cell-fill — it takes the archive's "Broad Coverage Cash Yield Survival" and swaps ZSCORE for IND_ZSCORE, a substitution already tested independently on the book anchor — so it adds no new economic content and is exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

The claim that asset composition is meaningful only relative to sector while obligation coverage is an absolute solvency test is a genuine, falsifiable restriction rather than a normalization tweak, and the two legs are placed on comparable unit-variance scales so the expression matches the hypothesis.

This is the archive's "Collateral Quantity And Illiquid Productivity" with ZSCORE replaced by IND_ZSCORE, a one-operator variant whose motivation ("both legs are asset-composition, so neutralization should help more") is an untested rationalization rather than a new mechanism.

Stacking two already-validated one-operator refinements (rank-squaring from "Deep Value Concentrated Survival" and industry neutralization) onto a cash anchor already tested in "Broad Coverage Cash Yield Survival" is pure recombination, and squaring a uniform rank is only a mild reweighting, so any gain would be uninterpretable as evidence for either idea.

Adding a persistence dimension to the survival composite is a real conceptual departure from the archive's static snapshots, but the expression takes the minimum of a *cross-sectional rank sum*, so it measures worst relative peer standing rather than the "weakest absolute balance-sheet reading" the hypothesis describes, and the three-year requirement will further thin an already ~12% sample.

A coverage-robustness check on the collateral leg is a legitimate diagnostic and the che/at choice does plausibly relax the binding lct/act constraint, but substituting one liquidity proxy for another in an otherwise identical flagship construct is a low-information variant that will mostly re-estimate a known result on a modestly wider sample.
